analysis:
The only changes in scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py are at head lines 720-721, 730, 811-814 and 828. They update two comments and drop the trailing ' required' token from the expected route-request regex for the cluster-release-checks and build-job route lines. This is an offline CI-workflow unit test. It adds no production provider, coordinator, crypto or attestation code, and no runtime code path touches the threat-model assets A-001 to A-020.

All other lines in the supplied units are unchanged context. They include assertions that pin CI safeguards: SAVE_CACHES is limited to master/dev pushes, persist-credentials is false, there are no secrets or backend credentials in the provider job, fixture caches are keyed by content hash with no restore-keys, and strict-cache applies on master. The relaxed route regex weakens only the test's pin on a route-requirement suffix. That suffix controls whether a runner lane is mandatory, which is an availability or scheduling concern. It is not a confidentiality or integrity control.

The corresponding change to provider-plan.yml or the route job is not in the supplied units, so I could not confirm the matching workflow edit. Whether the workflow still emits ' required' is an integration question, and the regex now accepts only the form without it. If the workflow was not changed accordingly, the test would fail rather than silently pass. T-041 (prefix cache) is not affected, because the test only checks CI cache save policy and no production cache behavior changes.

I found no concrete security regression. I did not examine the unchanged workflow files, and the patch excerpt was truncated at the final hunk. The range map is complete, though, and it lists only the small hunks above.
